The FOMC delivered a dovish pause, holding the federal funds rate at 2.25–2.50% and emphasizing “patience” amid slower household spending/business investment and muted inflation; market-based inflation compensation remains low. Implementation choices (IOR at 2.40%) are consistent with the floor system.

SLOOS context (Jan 2019) reinforces the cautious tone: banks reported tighter standards and wider spreads for C&I (including construction/land development) and CRE, weaker demand across business and residential real estate/HELOCs, and expectations for 2019 of tighter standards and softer demand. Some consumer categories were unchanged on standards, but overall credit supply tightened and demand softened, with banks anticipating deterioration in mortgages and nonprime consumer credit. These credit headwinds, together with the Financial Stability Report’s caution on leverage and risk premiums, temper the initial risk-on impulse from the dovish guidance—supportive for duration, only marginal for risk assets.

Adjusting for SLOOS, the net market tone is closer to neutral-to-slightly positive rather than clearly positive.
